title: Health Canada, Extreme heat and human health: For pharmacists and pharmacist technicians
license: Government of Canada publication; terms at https://www.canada.ca/en/transparency/terms.html
mapping_rule: Health Canada lists example drug classes without per-class reasons. Each class is mapped to ATC prefixes or ingredient names with a one-line reason. Ambiguous classes take the narrower reading. Committed before the first evidence run.

phrases.reason: Antipsychotics N05A. Lithium (N05AN) is listed separately by Health Canada and counted under its own phrase.
All antidepressants N06A: SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, and others such as bupropion, mirtazapine, and trazodone. Health Canada gives no narrower class.
Antiepileptics N03A, which includes gabapentin and pregabalin (N03AX) even when prescribed for pain.
Cholinesterase inhibitors N06DA. Narrower reading: memantine (N06DX) is an anti-Alzheimer agent but not a cholinesterase inhibitor, which Health Canada specifies in parentheses, so it is excluded.
All antiparkinson agents N04, anticholinergic and dopaminergic.
ACE inhibitors plain (C09A) and in combinations (C09B). Narrower reading: ARBs (C09C, C09D) are not named by Health Canada and are excluded.
Calcium channel blockers C08 and beta blockers C07.
